paper.title: Variable Neighborhood Search for Large Offshore Wind Farm Layout Optimization

paper_problem.decision_variables: binary selection of exact zone-wise turbine cardinalities from legal candidate positions
paper_problem.objective: maximize free-wind AEP minus foundation cost divided by energy price plus symmetric pairwise wake losses
paper_problem.constraints: fixed cardinality by zone and pairwise minimum spacing
paper_problem.wake_model: Jensen top-hat with partial overlap; fixed-neighbor wakes use quadratic superposition and movable pair losses use the paper linear matrix approximation

method.initialization: all-active PDSP-inspired progressive worst-contribution removal with exact zone cardinalities and deterministic feasibility completion
method.local_search: best-improvement 1-opt followed by nearby 2-opt with O(n) matrix deltas

formal_protocol.shake_ablation: ten shake strategies on official B, D and E, one hour each
formal_protocol.foundation_study: ten sites by low, high and no foundation-cost mode, one hour each
formal_protocol.long_run: ten no-foundation sites, one ten-hour run each with 1, 2, 5 and 10 hour checkpoints
formal_protocol.repeat_count: the paper does not report independent repeats; one deterministic declared seed is registered per paper-native run

missing_and_declared_completions.completion: reconstruct Algorithms and Sections 3.1-3.4 from the paper
200 and 40 EUR/MWh respectively represent low and high foundation-cost influence
use a lexicographically dominating 1e8 MWh-equivalent per violated metre and validate final feasibility independently
use k=0.04 and 5 new-turbine rotor diameters for official sites
remove five percent of each current zone excess, decreasing naturally to one
try single-position repairs, then deterministic greedy maximal spacing sets over the PDSP priority and 31 counter-keyed alternative orders

missing_and_declared_completions.field: VNS radii, neighborhood count, candidate caps and conic angle
missing_and_declared_completions.completion: three radii of 3D, 5D and 8D; published shake families; 128 one-opt candidates; 32 two-opt turbine pairs by 16 candidates; 60 degree conic wedge
publish deterministic counter-keyed events and explicit seeds

paper_data_conflicts.paper_dataset_fact: README says 26 and 8, while info.json and its printed 8 MW/km2 zone-area rule imply 26 and 14
paper_data_conflicts.resolution: use 26 and 14 from the data/formula-consistent info.json path and preserve the conflict in code and contract

paper_data_conflicts.paper_fact: the paper describes a directed k-by-k matrix while the binary objective uses both Iij and Iji
paper_data_conflicts.resolution: store one packed symmetric value Iij+Iji; this is algebraically identical for the stated objective

hpc.executor: one persistent all-core team per optimization
parallel_regions: fixed-neighbor preprocessing over all candidate positions
packed pairwise wake-matrix construction over all candidate rows
PDSP contribution construction and batch updates
sufficiently large 1-opt, 2-opt and deterministic shake candidate-delta sets
hpc.adaptive_granularity: short candidate-delta domains stay in the calling thread to avoid synchronization slowdown; large domains use all workers
hpc.data_layout: contiguous fixed-wake states and memory-mapped packed symmetric float matrix
ordered_dependencies: VNS neighborhood update and incumbent retention
hpc.determinism: counter-keyed random events, fixed-index parallel writes, stable reductions and ordered state commits

claim_boundary: Academic paper/data reconstruction; not author VNS source, unpublished parameter replay, original random bitstream, or numerical replay.
